citations.field: PDF pp.1289–1290, printed pp.1274–1275; 巴部 headword and continuation
citations.text: The 巴 headword gives bā, 帮纽、鱼部; 帮纽、麻韵、伯加切. Its glyph line labels the first form 《说文》小篆, followed by two 漢 forms and a 楷书 form. The account says the graph is pictographic and resembles a large snake in the 巴部; it describes the earliest displayed form as 《说文》 small seal, proposes a giant snake as the original referent, and transmits the traditional elephant-eating-snake story. The continuation on printed p.1275 says later uses such as 尾巴、下巴 and others are loans with no apparent connection to the original sense. This is the book’s attributed account, not independent paleographic confirmation; it concerns 巴 itself, not a direct claim about 吧.
